Bowers gained a double, winning the 100 yards and 220 yards, with Frank Simmons 4th. The 440 yards was an easy win for Frank Webb, with Tommy Morrell, taking up sprinting, 2nd.
High Jump.—1, Wise (BH), 5ft. 1½ins.; 2, Reynolds (Dkg.), 5ft.; 3, Savage (BH), 4ft. 11ins. Long Jump.—1, Read (Dkg.), 18ft.; 2, Carter (Dkg.), 17ft. 0ins.; 3, Simmons (BH), 17ft. 8¼.

Bishop, 2 min. 10 secs. 1 mile: Herbert, 4 min. 52 secs., 3rd, Short Relay (4 x half a lap), 1st, Epsom; 2nd, Bels. (Grimshaw, Simmons, Walden and Broadbent); 3rd, Bel, Juniors (Marshall, Baker, Mullen, Sexton).
Simmons of the home club was first home in 16m. 35s., and he was followed by Frank Wright and the rest of our lads packed well, to give us the edge over the home team.
In a bunch close behind were Gebbett, Masters, Walker and Robinson with Rogers and Simmons of Mitcham. With two miles to go the leaders, together with 'ghost' A.

Grand packing by Hampshire, Cocks and Morrison who all finished within the space of a few yards (4th,5th,6th) clinched a fine victory for the Bels in this year's Championship.Simmons (21st) and Satchell (22nd) provided excellent support.

Simmons ran his hardest against the class opposition but was forced to concede 5 places. "Noddy" Edwards ran his usual gutty race hanging on desperately to his 8th position in the final straight to bring the team home 93 secs behind the winners.
Brian Kilby 52 seconds ahead, Simmons (the Derby No.1) on his heels and another three of the day's top runners, Rushmer, Holt and Jackson chasing hard.
Lionel Mann placed second in the Bedford County 10 mile championship held in conjunction with the Luton '10'. The race was won by Simmons of Luton in 50:01 with Lionel 4th in 53:15.

The glamour of the Decathlon was confirmed by the outstanding performances of the young American Bob Mathias and Milt Campbell who, together with Simmons, gave America a clean sweep and a new Olympic Record.
